title: After Hours Care
description: Know where to seek help when we are closed, from after-hours GP care to emergency services.
headings: Mater Hospital Brisbane Adult Emergency Department
text: Patient Information After Hours Care Know where to seek help when we are closed, from after-hours GP care to emergency services. Information for patients of Woolloongabba Medical Centre in Brisbane’s inner south. Need medical help now? Choose the safest next step. Call Clinic Hello Home Doctor — 134 100 13 HEALTH Emergency — Call 000 Choose the right next step Use the option that best matches what is happening now. Clinic open — Call reception Life-threatening emergency — Call 000 Clinic closed — Call Hello Home Doctor Unsure what care you need — Call 13 HEALTH When we are open During normal opening hours, contact reception on (07) 3217 3344 for appointment availability and advice about the most appropriate next step. For life-threatening illness or injury, call Triple Zero (000) rather than waiting for a routine appointment. For a life-threatening illness or injury Call Triple Zero (000) and ask for an ambulance. Queensland Health advises emergency care for symptoms such as severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, severe bleeding, major trauma or other life-threatening conditions. Call 000 Hello Home Doctor When the practice is closed, patients can contact Hello Home Doctor on 134 100 or use its online booking service. Hello Home Doctor is an accredited after-hours medical deputising service providing GP home visits and, where clinically appropriate, telehealth. Published consultation hours: Monday to Friday 6:00 PM–8:00 AM; Saturday from midday; Sunday and public holidays 24 hours. Its call centre is open 24 hours to receive and triage requests. Eligibility, service coverage, attendance times and bulk-billing conditions can vary. Hello Home Doctor advises patients to call 134 100 to confirm coverage and eligibility. This service is not for emergencies. Visit Hello Home Doctor → 13 HEALTH If you are unsure what level of care you need, Queenslanders can call 13 HEALTH — 13 43 25 84 . Registered nurses provide health assessment and advice 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Queensland Health care options Nearby emergency departments Princess Alexandra Hospital 199 Ipswich Road, Woolloongabba QLD 4102 · Emergency services operate 24 hours. Mater Hospital Brisbane Adult Emergency Department Raymond Terrace, South Brisbane QLD 4101 · 24-hour adult emergency service · 07 3163 8111. In an emergency, do not delay care while comparing hospitals or waiting times — call 000. After-hours questions What should I do in a life-threatening emergency? Call Triple Zero (000) and ask for an ambulance. Do not wait for a routine appointment when symptoms are life-threatening. What after-hours service can I use when Woolloongabba Medical Centre is closed? When we are closed, contact Hello Home Doctor on 134 100 or use its online booking service. It provides after-hours GP home visits and, where clinically appropriate, telehealth. Eligibility and coverage conditions apply. What if I am unsure which after-hours option is appropriate? If you are unsure what level of care you need, Queenslanders can call 13 HEALTH on 13 43 25 84 for health assessment and advice from registered nurses, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. title: Telehealth Information
description: Telehealth information covering suitability, Medicare eligibility, booking and when an in-person consultation may be needed.
text: Patient Information Telehealth Telehealth can support continuity when a face-to-face visit is not required, subject to clinical suitability and Medicare rules. Information for patients of Woolloongabba Medical Centre in Brisbane’s inner south. Booking telehealth Where a telehealth appointment is offered, book through the available HotDoc appointment options or call reception on (07) 3217 3344 if you are unsure which appointment type is suitable. A practitioner may recommend an in-person consultation instead if examination, testing or treatment cannot be provided safely by phone or video. Medicare eligibility For general practice telehealth, Medicare eligibility can depend on your relationship with our practice. Current Medicare rules allow GP telehealth items when, for example, you are registered in MyMedicare with our practice or you have had an eligible face-to-face Medicare service with us within the previous 12 months. Other rules and exemptions can apply. If you are unsure whether your telehealth consultation will be Medicare eligible, ask reception before the appointment. Preparing for the appointment Keep your phone nearby and make sure we have your correct contact number. Choose a private place where you can speak comfortably. For video appointments, use a device with a working camera, microphone and reliable internet connection. Have your medication list or relevant information available if the consultation relates to ongoing care. Prescriptions after telehealth Where clinically appropriate, an electronic prescription may be issued as an SMS or email token that you can present to a participating pharmacy. Telehealth fees Where a telehealth consultation is privately billed, our current fee schedule lists a weekday telehealth consultation at $65 with a Medicare rebate of $42.85, and a weekend telehealth consultation at $80 with a Medicare rebate of $42.85. Video telehealth items are also listed on the current fee schedule. Medicare eligibility and the final billing arrangement depend on the appointment and current Medicare rules. Reception can confirm this before your consultation. Telehealth questions When can telehealth be useful? Telehealth may be suitable for selected follow-up care, results discussions, medication reviews and healthcare planning when a physical examination is not required. Telehealth service → What happens if my doctor needs to examine me? If the concern cannot be safely assessed remotely, you may be asked to attend the medical centre or another appropriate in-person service. Book an appointment → Can prescriptions be issued after telehealth? Prescribing depends on the medication, your history and the doctor’s assessment. Some medicines require further review or an in-person consultation.
